messages:
sarah_support: FYI customer ACME-123 opened INC-9123 — they see intermittent 429s but console shows quota fully available the whole day. Repro steps attached.

sarah_support: curl we ran: 
```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-live-XXXX\" -d '{\"input\":\"hello\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# -> 429 {\"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\", \"code\":429, \"request_id\":\"r-9f7a3\"}
```

sarah_support: customer says this started after they scaled up usage ~48h ago. Console shows: Available tokens: 1,000,000; Used today: 1,200.

alex_devops: can you paste one of the enforcement request_ids and a timestamp? I want to grep logs. Also link to the account in the console.

sarah_support: request_id r-9f7a3 @ 2026-03-14T02:14:37Z. Console link: https://console.redwood.ai/customers/ACME-123/usage

jamal_prod: I pulled enforcement logs for that request_id: 
```
[2026-03-14T02:14:37Z] req=r-9f7a3 tenant=ACME-123 enforcement=DENY reason=token_bucket_missing key=5f4D2A3e
```

ingrid_sre: interesting: enforcement says token_bucket_missing not exceeded. That implies enforcement couldn't find an in-memory bucket and defaulted to deny. Does the console read from the same store?

jamal_prod: console reads the aggregated hourly counters from the rollup DB (timeseries-store). Enforcement checks the in-memory bucket cache populated by the quota-service which loads from Redis. If Redis load fails, enforcement may deny.

sarah_support: customer shows no Redis incidents. They have spikes in traffic but nothing obvious.

quota-bot: quota-aggregator alert: write_latency_p95 spike at 2026-03-14T02:02Z -> 8.7s; consumer_lag=0 for partition 12.

alex_devops: I ran this query against the rollup DB for the tenant: 
```
SELECT tenant_id, sum(consumed_tokens) as used FROM hourly_token_rollups 
WHERE tenant_id = 'ACME-123' AND ts >= '2026-03-14' GROUP BY tenant_id;
```
Result: tenant_id=acme-123 used=1200

ingrid_sre: note the tenant_id in rollups is lowercased. Enforcement log shows key=5f4D2A3e (hex with mixed case). Could be an encoding/normalization mismatch between services (old IDs vs new canonical).

alex_devops: oh. During the sharding migration last month we switched to storing tenant keys as raw bytes (preserve case) in Redis, but the rollup writer normalizes to lowercase for backward compatibility. If enforcement looks up Redis with raw-case key it might miss buckets that were written under lowercased keys (or vice versa).

jamal_prod: confirmed: in Redis I see two keys: 
```
quota:tenant:5f4d2a3e -> {tokens: 1000000}
quota:tenant:5f4D2A3e -> (missing)
```
Enforcement used raw-case 5f4D2A3e which does not exist; rollups aggregated to 5f4d2a3e.

sarah_support: so console shows available (reads 5f4d2a3e) but enforcement looked up 5f4D2A3e -> not found -> DENY. That explains the mismatch.

ingrid_sre: yep. Root cause: key normalization regression introduced in sharding migration. A few customers created tenant ids with mixed-case hashes from older provisioning which now fail under certain code paths.

alex_devops: plan: 1) hotfix enforcement to normalize keys on lookup (PR ready, small change) 2) run a one-off Redis pass to copy lowercased keys to raw-case counterparts for impacted tenants 3) schedule a backfill to ensure rollups and Redis align, and add tests.

ingrid_sre: I'll own the hotfix deploy. Patch is small: enforcement/db.go line 142, add strings.ToLower(key) before redis GET; adding unit + integration test.

jamal_prod: I'll prepare the redis data migration script. Quick mitigation: temporarily whitelist ACME-123 for 24h to avoid customer impact while we deploy.

sarah_support: I told the customer we've identified a key normalization issue and are deploying a hotfix + backfill, will follow up in 2h. 

ops_bot: rollout started: enforcement-hotfix v2.14 -> canary (deploy id d-7781)

alex_devops: post-deploy check: grep enforcement logs for request_id r-9f7a3 replayed with corrected lookup.

jamal_prod: ran migration script against staging then prod dry-run: 
```
for k in $(redis-cli --scan --pattern 'quota:tenant:*'); do 
  canonical=$(echo $k | sed 's/.*://; tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')
  if [[ "$k" != "$canonical" ]]; then
    val=$(redis-cli GET "$k");
    redis-cli SET "$canonical" "$val"
  fi
done
```
Dry-run found 18 keys with mixed-case variance, including ACME-123 key.

ingrid_sre: canary looks good. enforcement logs show normalized lookups and no DENY for ACME-123 on a replayed request. Ops, please schedule the full deploy and run migration.

ops_bot: rollout complete: enforcement-hotfix v2.14 -> global.

jamal_prod: migration started; copying keys now. ETA 12m.

sarah_support: updated INC-9123: root cause identified (tenant key normalization mismatch), mitigation applied (whitelist + hotfix + redis copy). Customer notified.

sarah_support: customer replied: "Thanks — errors stopped after a few minutes. Appreciate the quick response :clap:"

alex_devops: follow-ups: add integration test between rollup-writer and enforcement using mixed-case IDs, add alert for redis key entropy changes, and add reconciliation job to detect missing keys.

sarah_support: marking resolved for now, will re-open if customer sees recurrence. :thumbsup:
